correctness.rationale: The full matrix space admits an orthogonal Weyl basis; direct conjugation makes the measurement of each Weyl matrix an orthogonal phase-space character times the normalized curve ambiguity. Every nonzero cubic-curve difference has uniquely determined source parameter from its first two coordinates, giving p(p−1) singleton nonzero shifts and ambiguity modulus 1/p there. At zero shift cyclotomic irreducibility forces the cubic polynomial output frequencies to occur once each, hence permutation. After depressing a cubic, t³+ut with u≠0 has a collision because 3s²+v²=−4u has p−χ(−3)>2 solutions while at most two have v=0. Therefore the exceptional zero-shift frequency set has size p−1 (p≡1 mod3) or p²−1 (p≡2 mod3). Weyl orthogonality gives the stated rank, full kernel, and nonzero-shift singular band exactly. The finite-field checker reproduces difference and permutation arithmetic for primes 5–29, but the general proof is algebraic, not an extrapolation.

For its complete Gabor projector ensemble the operator-span rank and individual lost Weyl coordinates are mathematically natural identifiable-degree invariants. The exact p modulo three transition records permutation-cubic cancellation invisible to the elementary support difference-set count and distinguishes two arithmetic regimes. The full kernel gives a concrete tomography obstruction/benchmark. Its precise structural content is nonroutine though the constituent Weyl identity and cubic permutation lemma are classical; no wider nonlinear phase-retrieval claim is made.
